title.narrative: Validating the commercial beta launch of Inuka mental health coaching in Kenya

description.narrative: Stress, worry and mental illness is one of the key challenges the world faces. Each year, one in five people suffer from depression or anxiety. In Africa, this is exacerbated by problems like youth unemployment, poverty and forced migration, negatively affecting people’s lives, physical health and society at large. Clinical coaching for mental health is nearly absent in African countries like Kenya: only 50 psychiatrists are available to support a population of 42 million people, leading to less than 10% of the population receiving the mental support they need. Furthermore, there’s a cultural stigma on mental health issues and seeking mental health coaching, causing millions of people to not receive the health coaching they need most in order to improve their well-being. To address this problem, Dutch company Inuka Coaching, a spin-out of Philips HealthCare Africa Innovation Hub, has developed an anonymised mental health mobile app chat service to offer mental health coaching to prevent and improve mental wellbeing of people in Africa. The chat services are offered by training ordinary people from local communities to provide personal coaching based on the proven Inuka-Method. To prepare for scale up investments in Africa, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provided support to Inuka Coaching and its Kenyan subsidiary, the Mental Wellbeing Company, to validate and further develop the MVP of the Inuka service in Kenya. The project included testing 3 different beta versions amongst 194 test users, training local people to become coaches and creating awareness amongst community leaders and the general public about mental wellbeing. The project supported 5 direct jobs (of which 3 new), 17 indirect jobs with local partners and contributed to sustainable knowledge transfer by training 32, including 5 employees and 28 potential mental health coaches, of which 5 are now active as a coach. Furthermore the project has led to increased awareness about mental health care and coaching in the country: via social media campaigns more than 1.000.000 Kenyan people were reached and more than 60.000 people referred to the Inuka website for more information. The validation was successful and further scale-up activities are currently being prepared which will hopefully result in at least 30 new direct jobs, 500 active coaches and improved access to mental wellbeing services for 150.000 Kenyans.
